newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: INFLATION RAISES CZECH RAIL CORRIDOR COST-MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: INFLATION RAISES CZECH RAIL CORRIDOR COST-MINISTER.

text.p: Construction costs of a high-speed rail link between Germany and Austria via the Czech Republic will exceed the 24.5 billion crown budget by up to seven billion, Transport Minister Martin Riman said on Tuesday.
Speaking to reporters after a ministers' meeting, Riman said the final stages of the construction might also stretch beyond the planned deadline in the year 2000 due to the increased costs.
"The costs will be increased, above all, due to inflation," Riman said.
He added that inflation expectations were not included in the original budget. Inflation was an average 8.8 percent in 1996 and is forecast at around 8.5 percent this year.
Riman did not give more details, and said it had not been decided how the increased expenditure would be financed.
The government has agreed a financing package for the 24.5 billion with a mixture of state subsidies, state-backed and unguaranteed loans.

The corridor, an upgrade of existing tracks, will run from the northern border with Germany through Prague to the south-eastern town of Breclav and then to Vienna. Trains should run at a top speed of 160 km (100 miles) per hour.
The Czechs are also building a second corridor, due to be finished in 2003, south from the border with Poland to meet the first corridor in the city of Brno.
